ILLNESS AND MEDICATION  
   
20 Some illnesses that can affect driving  
20.3 Depression
Depression affects the capabilities of the driver:
Increasing distractions. The driver focuses all his attention on his thoughts and neglects the surroundings.
Making valuable information become lost or irrelevant. The driver fails to detect significant information needed for safety and requiring driver reaction, especially in more complex situations.
Increasing insecurity. Depression interferes in the decision-making process, so the driver can make mistakes or act unpredictably.
Increasing the propensity for sleepiness and fatigue. It is advisable not to drive at night or in environments where road monotony may occur or for long periods of time.
Increasing irritability and anxiety. A trivial event can provoke a disproportionate reaction by the driver.
In addition, there is usually the need for psychotropic drugs, which can directly affect the ability to drive.

4.2.3 The tread pattern
The tread pattern is the set of grooves in the tread of a tire. In addition to gripping the road surface, it must guarantee good drainage away of the surface water from the tyre. The adhesion between the tyre and the road is reduced when the tyre is worn.
All tyres, (including retreads) must always comply with the legal requirements. 1.0 millimetres for vehicles in categories M2, M3, N2, N3, O3 and O4.

8 Speed limits are a necessity
 
Speed limits are not capricious. There are numerous factors that determine the implementation of a certain speed limit being imposed, (for example; the designated speed, the acceptable degree of congestion, the demands of existing traffic, etc.) The aim of a set speed limit is to allow vehicles to travel with the maximum guarantee of safety and fluidity.
One of the most important criteria is the designated speed of the road (the maximum safe speed that can be maintained on a section of road under favourable conditions). This means that a road is designated to be used at a certain generic or specific speed limit and traffic is not allowed to do a higher speed than that specified. To do otherwise means that safety will be compromised.

The driver of an automobile or a special vehicle with a weight in excess of 3,500 kg MAM will have to comply with the following rules:
In two-way roadways, with three lanes –one for either direction and a centre lane, where the lanes are defined by longitudinal broken lines, you must travel in the lane located to the right and never in the lane to the far left.
The centre lane is a shared lane, for use by vehicles overtaking (in either direction) and for turning left.
(Página 162 del manual 'Learning to drive')
